title: Collapse the edit-distance copy the wave's reservations forced
action: Cell csc-2 added `flag_distance` to router.rs — a second Levenshtein beside `catalog::distance` — and recorded WHY in a doc comment on `nearest_flag`: catalog.rs was reserved by sibling cell csc-3 for that wave, so widening the private helper's visibility was not csc-2's file to touch. Both reservations are released now. Make `catalog::distance` pub(crate), delete `flag_distance` from router.rs, point `nearest_flag` at the shared helper, and remove the deviation note from the doc comment (keep any sentence that explains what nearest_flag is FOR — only the 'why there are two copies' clause goes). Confirm no third copy of the same routine exists before finishing. The refusal bytes must not move: csc-2's three router tests, including the nearest-spelling suggestion for `state route --lane-value`, all still pass unchanged.

truths: Exactly one Levenshtein implementation remains in the crate
The refusal messages csc-2 shipped are byte-identical
The doc comment no longer claims a duplication that is gone
The full declared test suite is green

trace.outcome: Made catalog::distance pub(crate); router.rs's nearest_flag already called it directly via a tangled sibling commit, so only catalog.rs needed a change
